patients.summary: Graphic designer with childhood-onset generalized epilepsy on phenytoin, HIV (stage 3, 2016) on Biktarvy and recurrent severe depression who joins in 2018; central DI is diagnosed in 2019 and a folate-deficiency anemia recurs. Later a pregnancy with DI exacerbation, a seizure-related fall with TBI after stopping medicines (2023), cerebral toxoplasmosis at CD4 50 (2024), and a suicide attempt plan with psychotic depression (2026).

procedures.procedure: Office visit, new patient, high MDM

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT — establishing care

27 yo woman, graphic designer, lives in Holyoke with a roommate. Leaving her prior primary care office; wants one place that can coordinate her specialists.

HPI / PMH as she tells it:
1. Epilepsy since childhood, generalized seizures. Phenytoin 300 mg at bedtime for roughly three years now, before that other meds she can't name. Last seizure was in the spring of last year. Sees an outside neurology group about once a year.
2. HIV, diagnosed 2016. She says her count was very low when it was found ("stage 3"). Followed by an ID clinic, which moved her to Biktarvy earlier this spring; she does not remember the name of the earlier combination. Says she is taking it.
3. Depression, recurrent, with two bad episodes in her early twenties. Sertraline 100 mg has kept her steady. No psychiatrist currently; no hospitalizations. Denies SI today.
4. Folate deficiency after methotrexate in 2016 — she was given methotrexate for an ectopic pregnancy, which then ruptured and she ended up with a laparoscopic salpingectomy. Has taken folic acid 1 mg daily since, plus a prenatal vitamin ("I want a baby someday").

PSH: lap salpingectomy for ruptured ectopic 2016; D&C 2017.
Meds: phenytoin ER 300 mg qHS; Biktarvy 1 tab daily; sertraline 100 mg daily; folic acid 1 mg daily; prenatal vitamin with iron daily.
Allergies: SULFA ANTIBIOTICS — anaphylaxis. Latex — contact dermatitis.
FH: father epilepsy. Mother RA and type 2 DM. Sister with major depression. Maternal aunt breast cancer at 45.
SH: never smoker. Drinks occasionally at social events. No drugs. Works as a graphic designer, mostly from home.

ROS: negative except as above. Sleep ok. Appetite ok.

Exam: vitals as charted. Well-appearing, pleasant, good eye contact. HEENT unremarkable, oropharynx clear, gums normal. Neck supple, no adenopathy. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, healed laparoscopic port scars. No edema. Neuro: alert, fluent, CN grossly intact, gait normal. Skin without rash.

PHQ-9 8.

A/P:
- Epilepsy, controlled. Continue phenytoin. Will get neurology records; level at next visit.
- HIV on Biktarvy — ID manages ART. Requesting their most recent note with CD4/VL.
- MDD, recurrent, severe by history, currently stable on sertraline 100. PHQ-9 mild range. Continue; return 6 months or sooner.
- Hx drug-induced folate deficiency — continue folic acid.
- Health maintenance: CBC, CMP, lipids, TSH, hep C Ab, hep B sAg/sAb today. Pap and vaccines at a physical next month (she would rather not do the Pap today). Pneumococcal and meningococcal vaccines indicated with HIV.
- Records release signed for prior PCP, ID, neurology.

Return ~6 weeks for physical.

documents.title: Records Request
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Release of information signed by patient. Requests faxed to prior primary care office, outside infectious disease clinic and outside neurology group for last 2 years of notes, labs and med lists.

documents.title: Your recent labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Hi Gretchen,

Your blood counts, kidney and liver tests, cholesterol and thyroid all look fine. Hepatitis C and hepatitis B infection tests are negative.

One thing to act on: your hepatitis B antibody is negative, which means you are not protected against hepatitis B. With HIV we recommend the vaccine — it is two shots a month apart. We can start it at your physical along with the pneumonia and meningitis vaccines.

See you on the 29th.

documents.title: Infectious Disease Clinic Note (dated 2018-04-10)
documents.author: infectious disease
documents.body:
OUTSIDE INFECTIOUS DISEASE CLINIC — office note, date of service 04/10/2018

Reason: routine HIV follow-up after regimen change.

27F with HIV diagnosed 2016, AIDS-defining CD4 at diagnosis (stage 3), no opportunistic infections. Switched to bictegravir/emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide in February for simplification. Tolerating well, no GI upset. Reports she misses "maybe one a month."

Other: epilepsy on phenytoin (neurology), depression on sertraline (PCP). Allergies: sulfonamides — anaphylaxis; latex.

Labs today: CD4 310 cells/uL. HIV-1 RNA not detected (<20 copies/mL).

Assessment: HIV, virally suppressed on current ART. CD4 above 200; no prophylaxis needed.
Plan: continue Biktarvy. Labs and visit every 6 months. Vaccines through PCP.

— Infectious Disease attending

documents.title: Neurology Note (dated 2017-08-29)
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE NEUROLOGY — follow-up, DOS 08/29/2017

Generalized epilepsy since childhood. One generalized tonic-clonic seizure this spring after a stretch of poor sleep; none since. Taking phenytoin 300 mg nightly. Exam nonfocal. Gum exam normal.

Plan: continue phenytoin 300 mg qHS. Seizure precautions reviewed. Return 1 year.

documents.title: Prior Primary Care Records
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Records received by fax from prior primary care office, 22 pages. Problem list: epilepsy, HIV, depression, history of folate deficiency after methotrexate (2016). Surgical: laparoscopic salpingectomy 2016, D&C 2017. Med list matches current. Allergies sulfa (anaphylaxis), latex. No immunization records included. Scanned to media tab; abstracted for PCP.

reports.text: Specimen: cervical, liquid-based. Adequacy: satisfactory for evaluation; transformation zone component present. Interpretation: negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy.
reports.conclusion: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy (NILM).

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam. Feels well. No seizures. Mood steady. Taking all meds ("almost always" for Biktarvy). LMP 2 weeks ago, cycles regular.

Reviewed ID note from April: CD4 310, VL undetectable. Neurology note from last summer reviewed.

Exam: vitals as charted. Gen well. HEENT normal, gums normal. Neck no nodes or thyromegaly. Breasts symmetric without masses. Heart RRR. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. Pelvic: normal external genitalia, cervix without lesions, Pap obtained (nitrile gloves — latex allergy). Ext no edema. Skin normal.

A/P:
- Health maintenance: Pap today — with HIV, yearly Paps for three years, then every 3 years with HPV testing if all normal.
- Vaccines today: PCV13, Heplisav-B #1, MenACWY #1. Nurse visit in a month for Heplisav #2; PPSV23 and MenACWY #2 at 8 weeks.
- Epilepsy, HIV, depression: stable, as before.
- Follow-up in about 6 months.

documents.title: Pap result
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Hi Gretchen — your Pap smear was normal. The doctor would like to repeat it next year (yearly for three years is the recommendation for you). Reminder that your second hepatitis B shot is due around June 29.

documents.title: Immunization
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Heplisav-B dose 2 of 2, 0.5 mL IM right deltoid. Screening questions reviewed, no contraindications. Latex-free supplies used. Tolerated without issue. Series complete — antibody check can be done in 1–2 months per PCP.

documents.title: Immunizations
documents.author: RN
documents.body: PPSV23 0.5 mL IM L deltoid; MenACWY dose 2 0.5 mL IM R deltoid. VIS given. Pt waited 15 min, no reaction. PPSV23 booster due in 5 years (2023).

documents.title: Refill Request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy fax: refill request phenytoin sodium ER 100 mg caps, take 3 qHS, #270. Last fill by prior PCP. Pended for PCP — approved, 90-day supply with 1 refill. Pharmacy notified.

documents.title: Influenza Vaccine
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Flu vaccine 0.5 mL IM L deltoid. No egg or vaccine allergy. Latex-free bandage. Tolerated well.

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Six-month check. Mood "pretty good" — busy season at work, some stress with deadlines but sleeping fine. No seizures, no auras. Taking sertraline daily. Biktarvy most days, still the occasional missed dose. ID follow-up is in January.

PHQ-9 7. No SI.

1. MDD, recurrent, stable on sertraline 100 — continue.
2. Epilepsy — no seizures since spring 2017. Phenytoin level and albumin today. Continue 300 qHS.
3. HIV — per ID.
4. Flu shot done in October.
RTC 6 months / physical in spring.

documents.title: Phenytoin level
documents.author: PCP

documents.title: Infectious Disease Follow-up
documents.author: infectious disease
documents.body:
Outside ID clinic — visit 01/22/2019

Dear Doctor,

I saw Ms. Kelleher for routine HIV care. She remains on Biktarvy and reports good adherence over the holidays. No fevers, weight stable, no thrush.

CD4 342 cells/uL; HIV RNA not detected.

She completed the hepatitis B, meningococcal and pneumococcal series in your office — thank you.

Continue current regimen. Next visit in 6 months.

Allergies on file: sulfonamides (anaphylaxis), latex.

Infectious Disease attending

orders.reason: Polyuria and polydipsia, suspected diabetes insipidus

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit — Thirst/Urination
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: thirsty all the time, peeing constantly.

HPI: Started around February. Keeps a big water bottle at her desk and refills it "five or six times" a day. Up 3–4 times a night to urinate, which is new. Urine looks like water. No dysuria, no fever. No head injury, no new meds. No seizures. Mom has type 2 diabetes so she is worried about that.

Meds unchanged: phenytoin 300 qHS, Biktarvy, sertraline 100, folic acid, prenatal vitamin.

Exam: vitals as charted. Appears well hydrated, mucous membranes moist. Thyroid normal. Heart RRR, lungs clear. Abdomen benign. No edema. Neuro nonfocal; visual fields full to confrontation.

UA in office: very dilute, no glucose.

A/P: Polyuria/polydipsia. No glycosuria on the UA and a normal glucose on her April labs is expected — this does not look like diabetes mellitus. Dilute urine and sodium at the top of normal raise concern for diabetes insipidus. Lithium/hypercalcemia not in play; calcium pending. BMP, A1c today. Referring to endocrinology for evaluation. Told her not to restrict fluids on her own — drink to thirst. Call with confusion, vomiting or if she can't keep up with her thirst.

documents.title: Labs and endocrinology appointment
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Gretchen, your A1c and glucose are normal, so this is not sugar diabetes. Your sodium is at the high end of normal and the urine is very dilute, which fits with the hormone problem we talked about (diabetes insipidus). Endocrinology has you scheduled May 15. Keep drinking to thirst until then.

documents.title: RE: Labs and endocrinology appointment
documents.author: patient
documents.body: ok thank you. is that related to my seizures or the hiv? just want to know what to expect

documents.title: RE: Labs and endocrinology appointment
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Good question — we don't know yet. Endocrinology will sort out whether it's the pituitary signal (central) or the kidneys, and what might be behind it.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth twice daily

documents.title: Endocrinology Consultation (seen 2019-05-15)
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE ENDOCRINOLOGY GROUP — new consultation, 05/15/2019

Referred by: PCP. Question: polyuria/polydipsia.

History: 28-year-old woman with about three months of heavy urination and constant thirst. She estimates she now drinks roughly 6 liters a day and gets up several times overnight to void. No recent head injury and no surgery of any kind near the head. Background of childhood generalized epilepsy (phenytoin), HIV on ART, recurrent depression on sertraline, prior folate deficiency.

Allergies: sulfonamides (anaphylaxis); latex.
Meds: phenytoin, Biktarvy, sertraline, folic acid, prenatal vitamin.

Exam: normal, including visual fields and thyroid. Not volume depleted.

Labs today:
  Sodium 148 mEq/L
  Serum osmolality 300 mOsm/kg
  Urine osmolality 150 mOsm/kg

Impression: Central diabetes insipidus, currently inadequately controlled. Concentrated plasma with inappropriately dilute urine; the clinical picture favors a central cause.

Plan:
1. Start desmopressin acetate 0.1 mg by mouth twice daily.
2. Drink to thirst only — do not force fluids on desmopressin (risk of low sodium).
3. Sodium in one week through her PCP, please.
4. Follow up here in 3 months.

Thank you for this referral.
Endocrinology attending

documents.title: Lab Draw
documents.author: MA
documents.body: BMP drawn per endocrinology request (1 week on desmopressin). Pt reports thirst "way better already."

documents.title: Sodium result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your sodium is back in the normal range on the desmopressin — good. I've copied endocrinology. Happy birthday this week!

reports.text: Liquid-based preparation. Satisfactory for evaluation; endocervical/transformation zone component present. Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy. No organisms identified.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual. Doing well. Desmopressin has made a big difference — sleeping through or up once. Thirst normal. No seizures. Mood good, PHQ-9 6.

Interval: endocrinology 5/15 — central DI, desmopressin 0.1 BID. Sodium normal 5/22.

Meds: phenytoin ER 300 qHS, desmopressin 0.1 BID, Biktarvy daily, sertraline 100, folic acid 1, prenatal vitamin.
Allergies: sulfa (anaphylaxis), latex.

Exam: vitals as charted. Gen NAD. HEENT normal. Neck supple. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abd soft. Pelvic: normal external genitalia, cervix normal, Pap taken. Ext warm, no edema. Neuro nonfocal.

A/P:
- Central DI, on desmopressin — controlled clinically. Endo f/u in August.
- Epilepsy — stable.
- HIV — ID in July.
- MDD — stable on sertraline.
- Pap #2 of 3 yearly.
RTC fall for flu shot; 6 months.

documents.title: Pap result
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Normal Pap again this year. One more yearly Pap next year, then we can space them out.

documents.title: Endocrinology Follow-up (seen 2019-08-06)
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Endocrinology follow-up 08/06/2019

Central DI on desmopressin 0.1 mg BID. Polyuria largely resolved; nocturia once at most. No headaches, no swelling. Sodium normal at one week (PCP lab). Exam normal.

Allergies: sulfonamide antibiotics (anaphylaxis), latex.

Plan: continue desmopressin 0.1 mg twice daily. Drink to thirst. Sodium every 6–12 months, sooner with illness, vomiting or confusion. Return 1 year or as needed.

Endocrinology

conditions.label: Drug-induced folate deficiency anemia
conditions.note: Methotrexate-induced folate deficiency; recurrence with missed folic acid

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Follow-up — fatigue, gums.

S: Saw endocrinology in May (central DI, now on desmopressin, doing well on that). For the past ~2 months she has felt drained. Gums swollen and bleed with brushing. Eating the same as always; no change in bowels; weight steady. Periods regular, not heavy. On questioning she admits the folic acid "fell off" over the summer — she ran out and didn't refill, maybe 2–3 months. Taking phenytoin, desmopressin, Biktarvy and sertraline.

Mood ok, PHQ-9 7. No SI.

O: vitals as charted. Mildly pale conjunctivae. Gums erythematous and hyperplastic. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abd soft, no splenomegaly. No petechiae.

Labs 9/3: Hgb 10.2, MCV 102 (macrocytic). Folate 3 (low). B12 normal. Calcium 9.2. 25-OH vitamin D 30.

A/P:
1. Macrocytic anemia from folate deficiency — the same methotrexate-related folate deficiency she had in 2016, back now that she stopped her folic acid. Restart folic acid 1 mg daily — new script sent, 90 days with refills; set up auto-refill with her pharmacy. Recheck CBC and folate in 3 months.
2. Central DI — stable.
3. Epilepsy — no seizures.
4. MDD — stable.
Flu shot next month.

documents.title: Influenza Vaccine
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Influenza vaccine given IM R deltoid, 0.5 mL. No reactions. Latex-free supplies. Pt reports she is back on folic acid daily.

documents.title: Neurology Follow-up (seen 2019-11-19)
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
Outside neurology — annual epilepsy follow-up, 11/19/2019

Generalized epilepsy, seizure-free since spring 2017 on phenytoin ER 300 mg nightly. Interval diagnosis of central diabetes insipidus this year, on desmopressin. No sleep deprivation lately. Exam: alert, normal speech, no nystagmus, normal gait and coordination.

Allergies: sulfonamides, latex.

Plan: continue phenytoin at the current dose. Discussed seizure precautions and the importance of nightly dosing. Return in 1 year.

documents.title: Blood count recheck
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Great news — your blood count and folate are back to normal. Keep taking the folic acid every day; this is exactly why. Are your gums any better?

documents.title: RE: Blood count recheck
documents.author: patient
documents.body: yay. gums are a little better, bleeding less. energy way better
